1:1.t: Jude (Judas) is traditionally identified as a brother of Jesus and of James (Matthew 13:55). "Kept in Jesus Christ": the KJV's "preserved in Jesus Christ"; the Greek can mean "kept for Jesus Christ". "Sanctified": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "loved".

1:4.t: "The only Lord God and our Lord Jesus Christ": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "our only Sovereign and Lord, Jesus Christ".

1:5.t: "The Lord": the KJV's reading; some early manuscripts read "Jesus".

1:9.t: The dispute over Moses' body is not in the Old Testament; it was told in a Jewish writing, the Assumption of Moses. Compare Zechariah 3:2.

1:11.t: See Genesis 4:3-8, Numbers 22-24 and Numbers 16. "Korah": the KJV's "Core".

1:12.t: "Love feasts": the KJV's "feasts of charity", shared meals of the early church, often with the Lord's Supper.

1:14.t: A quotation from 1 Enoch 1:9, a Jewish writing from before Christ. Jude quotes it as a true prophecy without making the whole book Scripture.

1:22.t: The Greek text of these verses varies in the manuscripts; some have three groups instead of two.

1:3.t: "Once for all entrusted" (Greek hapax paradotheise): the faith was handed down by the apostles once, complete.

1:19.t: "Follow mere natural instincts" (Greek psychikoi): the KJV's "sensual". See 1 Corinthians 2:14.

1:24.t: One of the best-known doxologies in Scripture. "Keep you from stumbling" (Greek aptaistous): kept from falling.
